article_title: New vocational GCSE subjects to be introduced in schools

tasks.prompt: What is the main purpose of the education reforms described in the article?
options: To introduce vocational GCSEs and expand work experience so education connects more clearly with careers
To remove all academic GCSE subjects from schools in England
To require every pupil to leave school and begin work at 14
To replace colleges with private training companies
tasks.correct_answer: To introduce vocational GCSEs and expand work experience so education connects more clearly with careers
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הרפורמות נועדו להוסיף GCSE מקצועיים ולהרחיב התנסות בעבודה, כדי ליצור חיבור ברור יותר בין הלימודים לקריירה.

tasks.prompt: When are the new vocational GCSEs planned to be introduced in England?
tasks.explanation_hebrew: לפי הכתבה, המקצועות החדשים מתוכננים להיכנס לבתי הספר באנגליה בשנת 2029.

tasks.prompt: What does the phrase “a clear pathway” mean in the article?
options: A new walking route between schools and colleges
A rule that all teenagers must choose the same career
A structured route from qualifications to further study and work
A list of buildings that schools must construct
tasks.correct_answer: A structured route from qualifications to further study and work
tasks.explanation_hebrew: pathway בהקשר זה הוא מסלול מובנה שמאפשר לתלמיד להתקדם מלימודי GCSE להכשרה נוספת ולעבודה.

tasks.prompt: Who will set national standards for the new qualifications?
options: Individual schools
Local employers
Further education colleges
Ofqual
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הרגולטור Ofqual יקבע את התקנים הארציים כדי שהציונים יהיו תואמים לרמת GCSE אחרים.

tasks.prompt: When the headteacher says the new courses must be “robust”, what does he mean?
options: They must be rigorous, reliable and properly supported.
They must use only heavy industrial equipment.
They must be shorter than existing courses.
They must avoid all examinations and assessment.
tasks.correct_answer: They must be rigorous, reliable and properly supported.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: robust כאן פירושו תוכניות חזקות ואמינות מבחינה לימודית, עם כוח אדם, מתקנים והערכה מתאימים.

tasks.prompt: What practical difficulty did several education leaders identify?
options: Students are legally forbidden to take vocational subjects.
Schools may lack specialist staff, facilities and sufficient resources.
Employers have already provided too many placements.
Ofqual has refused to regulate the new qualifications.
tasks.correct_answer: Schools may lack specialist staff, facilities and sufficient resources.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: מנהלים וארגוני חינוך הזהירו שיהיה צורך במורים מומחים, מתקנים מתאימים והשקעה מתמשכת.

tasks.prompt: Name two examples of subjects that could become vocational GCSEs.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לציין שני מקצועות אפשריים שמופיעים במפורש בכתבה.

tasks.prompt: Why might cooperation between schools and further education colleges help the reforms succeed?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להסיק כיצד שיתוף פעולה פותר בעיה מעשית, ולהשתמש בפרטים מן הכתבה.
expected_points: Colleges may already have industry-standard facilities.
Colleges may have qualified technical and vocational staff.
Cooperation could make learning genuinely employment-focused while reducing the burden on schools.

tasks.prompt: Summarise the proposed vocational education reforms and the main concerns about implementing them.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: הסיכום צריך להזכיר את ה־VGCSE, יעד ההתנסות בעבודה, מטרת המסלול המקצועי ולפחות חשש מרכזי אחד.
expected_points: Vocational GCSEs are planned from 2029 alongside core academic subjects.
Employers are being asked to help create 200,000 work-experience opportunities.
The reforms aim to create clearer routes into college courses and work.
Concerns include staffing, facilities, funding and the risk of lowering expectations for some pupils.

tasks.prompt: Using evidence from the article, evaluate whether vocational GCSEs could improve education for teenagers.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להציג עמדה מאוזנת, עם ראיה אחת לפחות ליתרון וראיה אחת לפחות לסיכון או לקושי ביישום.
expected_points: Possible benefits include practical learning, confidence, career relevance and clearer progression routes.
Possible risks include shortages of specialist teachers, conversion costs and unequal steering of disadvantaged pupils.
The conclusion should weigh the benefits against the implementation concerns.
